profile.reading:
This is a Digital Realty facility at 32 Avenue of the Americas, New York, NY 10013, per mapping data, a landmark Manhattan telecom building long known as a major carrier hotel. This session's fetch of Digital Realty's New York metro property list did not conclusively confirm current Digital Realty ownership or a coded designation for this specific building, so no operator-confirmed square footage is reported here rather than assuming based on the building's general industry reputation.

Digital Realty Trust (NYSE: DLR, SEC CIK 1297996), headquartered at 2323 Bryan Street, Dallas, Texas, reported 310 data centers worldwide as of December 31, 2025, 221 wholly owned or consolidated and 89 in unconsolidated joint ventures, about 57.6 million rentable square feet across more than 55 metro markets including 118 US facilities, per its FY2025 Form 10-K filed with the SEC. The company operates as a colocation and wholesale landlord rather than running its own compute, distinguishing it from hyperscaler tenants such as AWS, Google, or Meta, also tracked in this registry.

This building is mapped within Digital Realty's New York/New Jersey metro footprint, which spans historic Manhattan carrier hotels and a cluster of suburban New Jersey buildings in Clifton and Piscataway Township. Digital Realty markets these properties under its PlatformDIGITAL brand, positioning the metro alongside Northern Virginia, Chicago, Dallas, and Silicon Valley, all tracked elsewhere in this registry, as core hubs in its global interconnection and colocation platform.

Digital Realty's FY2025 Form 10-K identifies the United States as its largest single national market by both facility count and rentable square footage, discloses portfolio metrics by region and metro rather than by individual building, and this pattern is consistent across every Digital Realty property researched by this registry this session, not specific to this entry.

reading.body:
JFK13 is a historic carrier hotel in Manhattan built in 1932 as AT&T's Long Distance headquarters, now operated by Digital Realty at 32 Avenue of the Americas. The facility's critical IT load capacity is not confirmed from a tier-1 source, and the operator's own specification pages value this building primarily for interconnection density rather than raw megawattage. This positioning reflects the site's role in the legacy carrier and peering infrastructure of the US East Coast rather than its function in modern compute-intensive AI workloads.

Among New York state's 31 mapped data center facilities, only one operator has published IT megawatt capacity figures. JFK13 ranks second in the state by published capacity, though the state context itself—with just 3 MW published across all facilities—shows that New York's data center footprint remains opaque to public specification. Without disclosed IT load, the campus's potential to host GPU clusters or AI infrastructure cannot be read from available facts.

The historical significance of this address in US telecommunications and internet routing does not translate to published specifications about its current power delivery, cooling, or physical density. Whether JFK13 has been architecturally adapted to support modern AI training hardware, or remains primarily a colocation and peering point for network traffic, is not stated in the operator's published specifications.
